title: Archive.org: The Web's Memory
description: Learn Archive.org: The Web's Memory in one minute.

hook.text: The web forgets. Pages disappear, links break, and digital history vanishes.

buildup.text: Brewster Kahle founded the Internet Archive in 1996 to preserve the web's history.

discovery.text: The Wayback Machine has saved over 800 billion web pages spanning nearly three decades.

twist.text: The Internet Archive also lends digital books, sparking lawsuits from publishers.

climax.text: Without Archive.org, most of the early web's history would be permanently erased.

punchline.text: One nonprofit saved the web's memory for everyone.

quiz.question: What does the Wayback Machine preserve?
options: Snapshots of web pages over time
